questions.q: Where does the SQS ARN needed to wire up S3 event notifications come from?
options: Snowflake's SHOW PIPES output, in the notification_channel column, since Snowflake already created and is listening to that queue
The output of SYSTEM$PIPE_STATUS
The CREATE STAGE statement's URL field
A value you invent yourself in the AWS console
questions.explain: SHOW PIPES reveals the notification_channel ARN, which must be copied exactly into the S3 bucket's event notification configuration in AWS.

questions.q: What happens if the ARN copied into the S3 event notification doesn't exactly match the pipe's notification_channel?
options: Files land in the bucket but nothing triggers the pipe — the automation silently doesn't work
Snowflake automatically corrects the typo
The load runs but with a warning logged
The pipe deletes itself
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly calls out that a typo in the ARN means files land and nothing happens — there's no automatic correction.

questions.q: What does SYSTEM$PIPE_STATUS tell you that SHOW PIPES alone does not?
options: The warehouse the pipe is assigned to
The SQL text of the pipe's COPY INTO statement
Live execution state, pending file count, and the last time the pipe received a file
The pipe's creation date
questions.explain: SYSTEM$PIPE_STATUS returns real-time operational JSON (executionState, pendingFileCount, etc.), while SHOW PIPES lists pipe definitions and their notification channel.

questions.q: Why should a pipe run under its own narrowly-scoped role instead of the admin role used to set it up?
options: Because admin roles cannot own pipes in Snowflake
Because pipes require a role named exactly 'snowpipe_role'
Because it makes the pipe run faster
Least-privilege: an unattended automation should only have the specific grants it needs, not broad admin access
questions.explain: The lesson frames this as the same instinct as scoping any service account tightly — insert/select on one table, usage on one stage, nothing more.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what are the two real UI moments shown in its screenshots?
options: Signing up for a Snowflake trial and logging in
Creating a warehouse and creating a database
Configuring the AWS S3 event notification, and checking the pipe's status/ARN via SHOW PIPES in Snowsight
Writing a COPY INTO statement and running a SELECT query
questions.explain: This lesson uses two real screenshots from the Getting Started with Snowpipe quickstart: the AWS-side event notification setup, and the Snowflake-side SHOW PIPES result.
